question: Identify the Navratna of Akbar’s court who played a pivotal role in the development of the classical genre of Hindustani music.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tansen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tansen**, also known as Miyan Tansen, was one of the nine gems (Navratnas) in the court of Emperor Akbar.
 
• He is widely considered as a pioneer in the development of the classical genre of Hindustani music.
 
• Tansen was known for his ability to create ragas and for his mesmerizing performances.
 
• He is often credited with composing several new ragas and perfecting the dhrupad style of singing.
 
• His contributions significantly shaped the future of Indian classical music, making him a legendary figure in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navratnas of Akbar's Court:**

 
 
• The Navratnas were nine extraordinary talents in Akbar's court, each excelling in different fields such as literature, music, and administration.
 
• Other famous Navratnas included Birbal, Abul Fazl, and Raja Man Singh.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**
 
 
• It is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music from the South.
 
• Hindustani music places a strong emphasis on improvisation and exploring all aspects of a raga.
 
 
 
• **Ragas:**
 
 
• A raga is a complex structure of musical notes used as a framework for composition and improvisation in Indian classical music.
 
• Each raga evokes a specific mood and is associated with different times of the day and seasons.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad:**
 
 
• Dhrupad is the oldest form of Hindustani classical music and is characterized by its solemn and spiritual nature.
 
• It often involves elaborate and intricate vocalizations and was popular in the royal courts of North India.
